sections.title: Wall Building
sections.description: Nehemiah travels to Jerusalem and builds the wall

sections.title: Renewal
sections.description: Reading of the Law and renewal of the covenant

sections.title: Organization and Reforms
sections.description: Dedication of the Wall and Nehemiah's reforms

events.title: Nehemiah hears about the condition of Jerusalem
events.description: Nehemiah, who is cupbearer to the Persian king Artaxerxes in the citadel of Susa, receives a visit from his brother Hanani and some men from Judah. They report that the survivors in the province are living in great distress and disgrace, and that the wall of Jerusalem has been broken down and its gates burned by fire. Nehemiah mourns, fasts, and prays to God.

events.title: Nehemiah asks the king for permission
events.description: King Artaxerxes notices Nehemiah's sad face and asks what troubles him. Nehemiah offers a silent prayer and then asks the king for permission to travel to Jerusalem to rebuild the city. The king grants his request, gives him letters to the governors, and authorizes him to obtain timber from the royal forests.

events.title: Nehemiah Inspects the Walls
events.description: Three days after arriving in Jerusalem, Nehemiah goes out at night with a few men to secretly inspect the walls. He rides along the ruins of the Valley Gate, the Dung Gate, and the Fountain Gate, seeing the broken-down walls and burned gates. He tells no one yet about his plans.

events.title: Rebuilding Begins and Opposition Arises
events.description: Nehemiah gathers the people and speaks of God's good hand upon him and the king's support. The people rise to build, and the work is divided among various families and groups. But Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem mock and oppose them. The enemies plan attacks, but Nehemiah organizes a defense where half build while the other half stand guard with weapons.

events.title: Nehemiah's Social Reforms
events.description: A cry arises from the people against their own Jewish brothers. Poor families have had to pledge their fields, vineyards, and homes as collateral, and some have sold their children into slavery to pay taxes. Nehemiah becomes angry and confronts the wealthy. He makes them return the land, money, and interest, and he himself gives up his governor's allowance for twelve years.

events.title: Sanballat and Tobiah Threaten Nehemiah
events.description: Sanballat and Geshem repeatedly try to lure Nehemiah to a meeting in the Valley of Ono to harm him, but Nehemiah sees through their plan and refuses to come. They send an open letter with false accusations that Nehemiah is planning a revolt. The prophet Shemaiah also tries to lure him into the temple, but Nehemiah reveals that he has been bribed by Tobiah.

events.title: The Wall Completed in 52 Days
events.description: The wall is finished in just 52 days. When all the enemies and surrounding nations hear about it, they lose heart because they realize this work was done with God's help. Nevertheless, Tobiah continues to send threatening letters and has many connections among Judah's nobles.

events.title: Ezra Reads the Law
events.description: The whole people gather in the square before the Water Gate. Ezra, the scribe, brings out the Law of Moses and reads from it from early morning until noon. The Levites explain the meaning of the law to the people. When the people hear the words of the law, they begin to weep, but Nehemiah and Ezra say that this day is holy and that they should rejoice, for the joy of the Lord is their strength.

events.title: Renewal of the Covenant
events.description: The people gather for fasting and confession. The Levites lead a long prayer that reviews Israel's history from Abraham to the exile, confessing the people's sins. Then they make a written covenant in which they commit to keeping God's law, not marrying foreign peoples, observing the Sabbath, paying the temple tax, and giving tithes and firstfruits.

events.title: Dedication of the Wall
events.description: The Levites gather from all over the region to dedicate Jerusalem's wall with joy, thanksgiving songs, and playing on cymbals, harps, and lyres. Two large choirs of thanksgiving march in procession along the wall in opposite directions and meet at the temple. Great sacrifices are offered, and the joy is so great that it can be heard from far away.

events.title: Nehemiah's Second Visit and Reforms
events.description: Nehemiah returns to Jerusalem after being with the king for a time. He discovers that Tobiah has been given a room in the temple, that the Levites have not received their share and have left their service, that the Sabbath is desecrated by trading, and that Jews have married foreign women. Nehemiah sets all these matters right with firm authority and asks God to remember him for his faithfulness.
